title: Root-space dimensions and independent Lie words
statement: For the generalized Cartan matrices and maximal contragredient quotient specified in records 532--533, compute a prescribed root-space dimension and independent representing words. No efficiency or canonical-basis requirement is present in the notebook.
status: As of November 2026: computationally determined degree by degree. Berman--Moody's 1979 formula covers symmetrizable matrices; the larger literal class is handled by finite recursive lowering maps as explained in the annotation. This is not recorded as an open demand for a uniform positive combinatorial formula. Earlier root-system and denominator occurrences are thematic predecessors, not exact previous formulations of this problem.

title: Three classical double-coset spaces
statement: Describe \(U(n)\backslash GL_n(\mathbb C)/U(n)\), \(B\backslash GL_n(\mathbb C)/B\), and \(U(n)\backslash GL_n(\mathbb C)/B\), with \(U(n)\) unitary and \(B\) the invertible upper triangular subgroup; the unitary interpretation is explicitly reconstructed.
status: As of November 2026: classical solved exercises. The invariants are respectively ordered positive singular values, a permutation in \(S_n\), and no invariant (one double coset). The three distinct questions share this problem entry. The earlier Bruhat occurrence 1979-483.1 is a related theorem, not an identical three-part question.

title: Integer Gelfand–Tsetlin arrays with four fixed top entries
statement: Count integer triangular interlacing arrays with fixed weakly increasing top row \(m_1,m_2,m_3,m_4\), including equality at every interlacing bound.
status: As of November 2026: solved by the type-A Weyl dimension product displayed in 1981-536.7 and the 1950 Gelfand--Tsetlin basis. The earlier 1976-415.5 and GP-1976-24 concern standard tableaux/Young-graph paths, a related but different branching graph; no exact recurrence of this fixed-integer-row question is present in the supplied index.

title: The type-A quiver formula for p-adic GL(n) multiplicities
statement: For standard induced representations of \(GL_n(F)\) on a fixed cuspidal line, express their irreducible Jordan--H\"older multiplicities through local intersection cohomology of the corresponding graded nilpotent/type-A quiver orbit closures. The notebook occurrence is an abbreviated allusion, identified through Zelevinsky's 1981 paper.
status: As of November 2026: proved in the specified GL(n) setting. Current direct sources are Solleveld's Theorem 5.4(b), his standard-module comparison Lemma 6.2, and Balodis's version-2 Theorem 3.9. First circulation and revision dates are separated in the occurrence. GP-1979-41 concerns the earlier Verma-module/Schubert Kazhdan--Lusztig problem; it is a related precursor, not this p-adic multiplicity question.
